content:
The number of applicants for the IELTS examination has been increasing day by day. In such a scenario, it is necessary to know what is real and what is not. Speaking is the most dreadful part for many aspirants. The various myths associated with speaking tests have been a source of concern. If you are looking for the best IELTS coaching centre in Cochin, there is no need to think twice, because Casper Academy provides the most effective strategies. In this article, we provide some myths and truths associated with the speaking test.

You Have to Agree to the Examiner’s Opinions

While having a conversation with the examiner, it is not mandatory to agree to what they say. Especially in situations in which you do not believe in their opinion. The only thing that matters is your ability to engage in fluent conversation. Your ideas are not important as long as you can communicate them fluently. If you want to disagree, acknowledge their view point and then present what you have in your mind. Casper’s IELTS training in Kochi gives you the opportunity for great preparation.

You Need to Speak in Native Accent

It is not mandatory to have a native-like accent to score a good band score in a speaking test. The examiner does not want you to speak like him/her. Your attention should be on your pronunciation, fluency, coherence, and the correct use of grammar. A good method to improve your speaking skills is to practice with your friends or family, or even your teachers. It gives an idea about the level of your skills, and where you need improvement.

Using Short Sentences is the Key

Many believe that the chances of committing errors are less while you use simple and short sentences. But the examiner evaluates your ability to form various kinds of sentence structures. Being the top IELTS institute in Ernakulam, we give intensive coaching that helps you to fluently speak in English. Using short sentences reduces your ability to use clauses and joining words. It puts restrictions on your ability to stand out in a conversation. In worst cases, instead of creating a good impression, it may leave a negative impression. Thus use all kinds of sentences.

You Cannot Ask the Examiner to Repeat the Question

A major fear that exists in the minds of the candidates during the test is that they have to answer every question- even if they haven’t heard the question clearly. This is entirely false. You can ask the examiner to repeat the question for clarification. The chances of answering correctly are definitely increased when you can get a proper idea of the question.

Speaking Test is Simple

Since there is no writing present in this part, some people believe that it is easy to score a good band score in the speaking part. But the fact is, every test has its own challenges. The evaluation criteria of the speaking test is a bit more than engaging in a conversation. You should ensure that your ideas are clearly communicated, have fluency and pronunciation.
